comments.body:
OPERATOR REQUIREMENT + PRE-IMPLEMENTATION VERIFICATION: per-pass model parity on cutover.

REQUIREMENT (operator, this run): after the Bedrock cutover the code-review agent must use COMPARABLE models per pass — Pass-1 on opus for many/all of its criteria, Pass-2 (verify) and Pass-4 (coach) on sonnet.

VERIFIED AGAINST LANDED CODE (worktree feat/llm-provider-seam @ 8465873ec). As written this story CANNOT satisfy that requirement, for three INDEPENDENT reasons:

(1) Code review has NO per-pass model split today, on ANY provider. src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml (190 lines) declares no `model:` and no `model_ladder:` on any step, so base/round_a/round_b (Pass-1), verify (Pass-2, `temperature: 0` at :155) and coach (Pass-4) ALL resolve to cfg.model via resolve_model (step > workflow > config). The sonnet downgrade this requirement assumes exists ONLY in plan-review: _verifier_cfg (plan_review/__init__.py:46-70) -> review_kernel.resolve_verifier_model. Consumers of resolve_verifier_model are plan_review/{__init__,xcheck,orchestrator,workflow_ops}.py and completion.py — code_review calls it NOWHERE. So the code-review agent currently runs Pass-1, Pass-2 AND Pass-4 all on claude-opus-4-8. Satisfying the requirement is therefore NEW WORK, not preservation of existing behaviour — worth stating plainly because "use comparable models" reads like a no-op parity ask and is not one.

(2) The one downgrade rule that DOES exist inverts on Bedrock. review_kernel/verify.py:269 is `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or verifier_default)`, with default_model = "claude-opus-4-8". ANY Bedrock id ("bedrock:us.anthropic....") is a non-default value, read as an explicit operator choice, and returned unchanged. Consequence: on cutover plan-review's Pass-2/Pass-4 STOP downgrading and follow Pass-1 onto whichever single Bedrock model REBAR_LLM_MODEL names. This story's Scope is exactly that one env var ("infra/compose/ — the bot service's REBAR_LLM_MODEL"), i.e. ONE knob for FOUR passes.

(3) Bare `claude-*` names route to ANTHROPIC, not Bedrock. config.py:333-341 _PROVIDER_PREFIXES maps prefix "claude" -> "anthropic". plan-review.yaml:62-65 sets Pass-1's model_ladder to bare [claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-8]. After a cutover that only re-points REBAR_LLM_MODEL, that ladder STILL resolves to direct Anthropic — a SPLIT-BRAIN where the Pass-1 finder keeps calling Anthropic while everything else is on Bedrock. Bedrock needs inference-profile ids (us.anthropic....) which match no prefix rule, so every ladder/step model must be rewritten provider-aware, not merely re-pointed.

NOT A USABLE SECOND KNOB: cfg.bedrock_model_id / REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID is parsed from env (config.py:521, 633-638) and documented in docs/env-vars.md:55 but is READ BY NOTHING — no consumer in src/ or tests/. It is dead config as landed by S3 and cannot carry a per-pass mapping until it is wired up. (Filing that as its own defect.)

WHY THIS IS URGENT, NOT COST-COSMETIC — measured this run, in the project account 896586841071/us-east-1:
- Pass-2 pins temperature=0 (code-review.yaml:155). us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 + temperature=0 -> ModelHTTPError 400 "temperature is deprecated for this model". Resolving Pass-2 onto an opus profile can HARD-FAIL the gate, not just overspend. S3's supports_temperature override (capabilities.py:95) lists opus-4-7 ONLY.
- us. AND global. opus-4-5 report cache_read=0 / cache_write=0 while billing full input; us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 caches. An opus-everywhere cutover also loses caching SILENTLY.
- Conversely a sonnet-everywhere cutover (DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID = us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6) silently DOWNGRADES Pass-1 from opus — a finder-quality regression no existing test would catch.
So both single-model cutovers are wrong, in opposite directions. This is exactly the gap the operator flagged.

PROPOSED AC ADDITIONS (this story, or a new sibling if the config seam turns out large):
- [ ] the cutover configures the Pass-1 and Pass-2/Pass-4 model ids INDEPENDENTLY
- [ ] a test asserts the RESOLVED model for each pass under a Bedrock config is the intended class (opus-family for Pass-1; sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4)
- [ ] no bare `claude-*` model id survives on any path the bot executes post-cutover (else it silently routes to Anthropic)
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real post-cutover vote's sidecar shows the per-pass model ids actually used, citing the change id

NOT fixed inside this story's current Scope because the requirement needs a config seam that does not exist (one env var cannot express four passes), and that seam is a design decision rather than an implementation detail — same class as 2682 (runner.py at the cap) and the providers.py 299/300 blocker on 343b. Raising it in the PLAN rather than leaving an implementer facing an unwinnable constraint.

comments.body:
BEDROCK CUTOVER MEASURED END-TO-END. A real plan-review ran on bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
against closed ticket 7468: 19 LLM calls, verdict BLOCK with a substantive plan-specific finding,
ZERO provider errors, zero degradations, no LLMUnavailableError. The provider path is functionally
sound. But THREE blockers were measured, and two of them I re-verified myself.

1. NO SINGLE-SCALAR SETTING REPRODUCES TODAY'S SPLIT. Baseline (direct Anthropic) = 41 opus (Pass-1)
   + 1 sonnet (Pass-2/4). The Bedrock run = 0 opus, 19 sonnet. REBAR_LLM_MODEL drives EVERY pass, so:
     - point it at Bedrock sonnet -> Pass-1 drops opus->sonnet, a CAPABILITY REGRESSION and a direct
       violation of the operator's 'Pass-1 opus-equivalent' requirement;
     - point it at Bedrock opus  -> Pass-2/Pass-4 lose the cost downgrade AND greedy decoding.
   => cc33 (class consumption at the runner) is a HARD PREREQUISITE for this story. Cutting over
   before it lands silently degrades review quality either way.

2. THE VERIFIER DOWNGRADE IS DEAD ON EVERY NON-BARE MODEL ID. I re-ran the pure function myself:
     claude-opus-4-8                        -> Pass-2 claude-sonnet-4-6                  downgraded=True
     anthropic:claude-opus-4-8              -> Pass-2 anthropic:claude-opus-4-8          downgraded=False
     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8   -> Pass-2 bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 downgraded=False
   verify.py:269 only downgrades on an EXACT match against the bare 'claude-opus-4-8'. Note the
   middle row: merely QUALIFYING the same model with its provider kills the downgrade. This is wider
   than Bedrock.

3. ESCALATION CROSSES PROVIDERS. I re-verified: models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6')
   returns [('claude-sonnet-4-6','anthropic'), ('claude-opus-4-8','anthropic')] — BARE ids that infer
   to provider 'anthropic'. On a context-limit error a Bedrock run silently escalates to DIRECT
   ANTHROPIC: a hard failure in a Bedrock-only container with no key, or silent Anthropic billing
   where a key exists. Not triggered in the run (no context-limit hit) — confirmed from the function,
   not observed live.

TWO FINDINGS THAT FAVOUR THE CUTOVER:
- PROMPT CACHING WORKS ON BEDROCK for both sonnet and opus (raw converse: cacheWrite then cacheRead
  on a repeated prefix; through rebar end-to-end: cache_read=542,723 / cache_write=6,239 over 19
  calls). Bug 7a79's silent no-op is a DIRECT-ANTHROPIC-path problem — Bedrock FIXES it rather than
  inheriting it. That is a cost argument for the cutover.
- TEMPERATURE: Bedrock sonnet accepts temperature=0.0; Bedrock opus rejects any value except the
  default 1.0 ('temperature is deprecated for this model'). So what is deprecated is TUNABILITY, not
  the parameter. rebar already withdraws it via capabilities overrides so opus will not crash — but
  the greedy Pass-2 pin (temperature: 0) is then silently INOPERATIVE. Keeping the verifier on
  SONNET preserves greedy verification; that is now a measured argument, not a preference.

CROSS-TICKET NOTE from sibling d23e (deprecate REBAR_LLM_MODEL) — recorded as a COMMENT, deliberately not edited into this ticket's plan, because redesigning a production recovery path is the operator's call and not a side effect of a deprecation ticket.

THIS TICKET'S KILL SWITCH IS NOT BROKEN BY d23e. Verified before writing this: _deprecations._scheduled(...) sets permanent=False with remove_in=_MAJOR — it WARNS, it does not remove — and d23e's window explicitly keeps REBAR_LLM_MODEL functional. So 'REBAR_LLM_MODEL back to anthropic:...' still restores voting, before and after d23e lands. No safety change, and no action is required for this ticket to work.

THE DURABILITY PROBLEM IS REAL THOUGH. d23e lands BEFORE this ticket (S8 is blocked behind eb58, which cannot close until d23e does), so as written this ticket would CREATE a new infra/runbooks/ occurrence of a variable that was deprecated one ticket earlier, and put it in infra/compose/ too. That runbook then rots when the variable is removed at the next major — and a recovery runbook that has rotted is discovered at exactly the wrong moment.

SUGGESTED, not imposed: express the kill switch in CLASS terms — configure the class slots, or set REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL — which is a strictly equivalent one-line operator action with the same blast radius, and does not depend on a deprecated surface. If you prefer to keep REBAR_LLM_MODEL because it is the shortest possible action under incident pressure, that is a defensible choice; in that case the runbook should say explicitly that it uses a deprecated variable and name the class-based replacement alongside, so the entry does not silently rot.

Either way the AC 'the kill-switch runbook entry exists under infra/runbooks/' stays satisfiable. d23e's docs criterion has been written so that nothing IT authors presents the deprecated variable as the recovery lever.

PLAN REVIEW OF THE REWRITE: BLOCK, 1 finding — AND IT IS A GENUINE SHOWSTOPPER THAT WOULD HAVE TAKEN
DOWN THE PRODUCTION GATE. Verified by me against the tree, not accepted on the reviewers word.

THE FINDING: the review-bot image does not install the [bedrock] extra, so the first Bedrock call after
cutover hard-fails.
    infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:83
        RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot
    pyproject.toml:133-135
        bedrock = ["pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2"]     <- a DISTINCT extra, not installed above
    src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:61-63
        from pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock import BedrockProvider
        except ImportError -> raise LLMConfigError
So the provider builder raises a typed config error on its first call. Fail-closed, correctly — but with
NO cross-provider fallback (this storys deliberate choice) that means the LLM-Review gate stops voting on
every landing the moment the cutover takes effect.

THE FAILURE SHAPE IS WORSE THAN A CLEAN ABSENCE, and this is the part worth remembering:
    pyproject.toml:93   reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]
The container HAS boto3. So the boto3-based region pre-check at bedrock_model.py:76-79 SUCCEEDS, and only
the provider import afterwards fails. A naive smoke test that checks "can this container reach Bedrock
with boto3?" would report healthy. The dependency is PARTIALLY satisfied, which defeats the obvious probe.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT UNTIL NOW — the same blind-spot pattern this epic keeps hitting:
[rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved all three gates run clean on Bedrock, 33 calls, zero direct-Anthropic.
That was LOCAL, in a dev env that installs every extra. A local proof cannot see a CONTAINER PACKAGING gap,
so its success gave false confidence about the image. The epics own recorded lesson applies verbatim: the
guard shared the bugs assumption. Neither the rewritten plan nor my brief to the rewriter caught this;
only the plan review, reading the plan against the packaging, did — which is the same thing that caught the
bedrock:Converse reversal on [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67] ("CI cannot see a plan/code contradiction").

THE PLAN IS BEING AMENDED rather than force-claimed. No --force. What it needs, per the reviewers
suggested fix and my verification:
  1. Add --extra bedrock to the reviewbot image install, so the provider package is present.
  2. A PRE-CUTOVER check in the ordering criterion that the import actually resolves INSIDE the container
     (e.g. `docker compose exec review-bot python -c "import pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock"`), because the
     boto3 region probe will pass regardless and therefore proves nothing about this.
  3. The check must run BEFORE the model flip, alongside the alarm proof — the same
     safety-net-first ordering the story already insists on. Discovering this after the flip means
     discovering it as an outage.

Note this also strengthens the existing ordering criterions rationale: the recovery path must be proven
before it can be needed, and so must the forward paths runtime prerequisites.

The plan review that raised it, and my own verification of it ('Verified by me against the tree'), both read the same declaration. This is the epic's own recorded lesson in a new costume — the check shared the claim's assumption. Note the irony: the finding correctly identified that a boto3-based probe cannot prove the import resolves, then itself concluded the import fails without running it.

Remove boto3 from the reviewbot extra, or let pydantic-ai-slim's bedrock extra grow a dependency beyond boto3, and the provider import breaks at gate time in production. This is the SAME fragility argument this plan already accepts when it rejects pointing REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE at /app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml because that file 'is present in the image only incidentally'.

* THE RISK FRAMING IS WRONG AND SHOULD NOT BE REPEATED: the cutover was never one flip away from taking the gate down. The safety-net-first ordering is still being honoured, but on its own merits (no cross-provider fallback by design), not because of an imminent packaging outage.

TWO FURTHER MEASUREMENTS FROM THE SAME PROBE.
* ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present in the container, len=108, evaluated INSIDE the container. Confirms the 'retained by design' position. (An earlier read of mine reported UNSET; that was a shell-quoting artifact — the variable was expanded on the HOST, not in the container. Discarded.)

comments.body:
INDUCED-VOTER_ERROR DRILL — METHOD PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE EXECUTION, so the induction cannot be rationalised after the fact. The criterion requires the method to be stated; stating it in advance is stronger.

WHY NOT THE OBVIOUS ROUTES.
* A CLOSED CHANGE is explicitly wrong: per [rebar:c943-1b38-d613-4013] a 409 'change is closed' deliberately does NOT emit VOTER_ERROR (voter.py:661-670 records the vote and returns 'skipped'). The criterion says so too.
* /rerun CANNOT REACH THE CHEAPEST SITE. app.py:293 looks the change up via GerritClient.get_change_event BEFORE enqueuing and returns 502/404 on failure, so a bad id never reaches the voter. And app.py:317 sets event['_rebar_force'] = True, which makes voter.py:456 SKIP the has_llm_review_vote dedup check entirely — so the :470 error site is unreachable on a forced rerun by construction.
* AN LLM OUTAGE (e.g. blanking the Anthropic key) is a poor instrument: an adapter failure produces a decision with a retryable gap_reason, which DEFERS with no VOTER_ERROR (voter.py:601-632) until the per-revision attempt budget is spent, and only then emits one at :637 — while ALSO casting a real -1 on a real change. Multiple cycles, real spend, and a false blocking vote on someone's change.

THE CHOSEN INDUCTION — the dedup-check transport failure at voter.py:470, reached through the REAL webhook path.
MEASURED PREREQUISITE: the bot addresses Gerrit at gerrit_base_url = http://gerrit:8080 — the compose SERVICE NAME on the internal network, not the public origin. And gerrit_client.py:116 wraps a transport failure as GerritError('... transport error: ...'), so a refused connection arrives as the same typed error a 5xx would.
So: append '127.0.0.1 gerrit' to /etc/hosts INSIDE the review-bot container. Outbound calls to http://gerrit:8080 then hit the container's own loopback, where nothing listens, and the FIRST Gerrit call in review_and_vote — the has_llm_review_vote dedup check at :456, which the webhook path DOES execute because no force marker is present — raises GerritError and fires _voter_error at :470.

WHY THIS IS THE NARROWEST AVAILABLE INSTRUMENT:
* ZERO LLM SPEND. The failure precedes any adapter call: the return is {'status':'error','stage':'dedup_check'}.
* NO VOTE IS CAST, and none can be — the code path returns before a decision exists, so there is no risk of a false +1 or a false -1 on a real change.
* NOTHING PERSISTENT IS EDITED. No config, no .env, no compose file, no Gerrit ACL, no IAM. /etc/hosts inside a running container is reverted by deleting one line, and is discarded anyway if autodeploy recreates the container — so the blast radius self-heals rather than needing cleanup to be remembered.
* IT EXERCISES THE WHOLE CHAIN AUTHENTICALLY, from the bot's MAIN process. That matters: observability.sh section 4 greps 'journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=<voter container>', so a marker written by a 'docker compose exec' process would NOT be captured — an exec'd probe is not a substitute for a real one, and would have silently proved nothing.

BLAST RADIUS, stated plainly: while the hosts entry is in place the bot cannot vote on ANY change, so a landing during the window gets no LLM-Review vote. That is recoverable with /rerun and is inherent to the criterion — it asks for the gate to fail once, on purpose. The window will be minutes, and will not overlap a change of mine that is awaiting review.

TIMING, from measurement rather than assumption: the observability probe is a systemd timer with OnUnitActiveSec=5min (rebar-observability.timer, confirmed on the host), and rebar-gerrit-voter-errors is period=300 / evaluation_periods=1 / threshold=0. So a single VOTER_ERROR should reach ALARM within roughly two probe intervals, and 'systemctl start rebar-observability.service' can force the publish immediately rather than waiting.

SEQUENCE: record the baseline alarm state and the current VOTER_ERROR count -> add the hosts entry -> trigger a real review by pushing a change -> confirm the VOTER_ERROR marker in the CONTAINER journal -> force the probe -> observe OK -> ALARM with timestamps -> remove the hosts entry -> /rerun and confirm a normal vote -> observe the alarm return to OK. The retry-after-restore observation doubles as evidence for the denied-access criterion's fourth clause.

# S8 — Cut the production review bot over to Bedrock Claude (dogfood, no cross-provider fallback)

## Context / Problem

The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main`, and today it runs against the direct Anthropic
API. The epic's premise is that our clients will predominantly reach Claude through Bedrock, so the
path rebar develops against is not the path rebar's users run; dogfooding closes that gap. State the
premise honestly: it is an asserted product judgement, not a measured one — no survey or citation
backs it anywhere in the epic. What IS measurable is the consequence: if Bedrock throttles,
mis-caches, or returns differently shaped structured output, we find out on our own repo before a
client does.

This ticket was written early in epic 061c and its original Scope and Approach have been overtaken by
the epic's own deliverables. The rewrite below replaces them. What changed:

* the per-pass model split it worried about **now exists in code**, so the cutover is a configuration
  act rather than a design problem;
* the single `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` knob it named is **deprecated** [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] and cannot
  express a per-class mapping, so it is no longer the instrument;
* the `observability.sh` alarm it listed as a deliverable **already shipped** under S4b;
* the Anthropic-key retirement it promised is **not expressible** against the current `.env` layout
  and would break the kill switch it also promises.

## What is already established — do NOT re-measure or re-build

* **The per-pass class split has LANDED.** `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` now
  declares `base: model: frontier` (:74), `round_a`/`round_b`: `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:92, :130),
  `verify: model: standard` (:174) and `coach: model: standard` (:209); `plan-review.yaml` Pass-1 is
  `model_ladder: [frontier]` (:70-71) and the verifier paths resolve `standard`
  [rebar:172e-b207-4c18-4243, rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74, rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0,
  rebar:3768-789c-11ed-48be, rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468]. The gate no longer reads a single
  `cfg.model` for all four passes. **The obsolete-plan hazard is therefore inverted from what this
  ticket used to say: the risk is no longer "one knob for four passes", it is choosing an instrument
  that COLLAPSES the split that now exists.**
* **No bare `claude-*` id survives on either gate's executed path.** The only remaining bare ids under
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` are `examples/review_skeleton.yaml:44` (an example, never executed by the
  bot) and JSX placeholders in `editor_assets/`. The split-brain this ticket previously warned about
  is closed.
* **Escalation no longer crosses providers.** `plan_review/sizing.py:400` `models_at_or_above` maps
  every at-or-above rung through its model class via `_rung_target`, which drops a rung it cannot name
  in the run's provider [rebar:7761-4b1a-e8c3-45a0]. A Bedrock-configured run escalates to Bedrock.
* **`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError` is now caught** (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:250,271`), so a
  Bedrock client-construction failure reaches rebar's typed failure path instead of escaping every
  `except LLMError` handler [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9].
* **Both region variables are ALREADY SET in the review-bot service.**
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:151` `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION: "us-east-1"` and `:157`
  `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: "us-east-1"`. They are NOT interchangeable and both are required: rebar's own
  knob threads into `BedrockProvider` while botocore reads only `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
  (`AWS_REGION` alone does not work on boto3/botocore 1.43.58), and IMDS supplies credentials but never
  a region [rebar:a574-7193-6a5b-48e9]. Verify, do not re-derive.
* **IAM is granted and exercised.** `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` +
  `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on `*.anthropic.claude-*` inference profiles, scoped to the instance
  role, verified by a real call rather than the policy simulator
  [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67].
* **The VOTER_ERROR alarm chain already exists and is live.** `review_bot/voter.py` `_voter_error()`
  writes a greppable line to journald; `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 (:113, :135) publishes
  `rebar/host:voter_errors`; `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` declares
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.voter_errors` = `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (`period = 300`,
  `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0`, :48-54); `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:110` documents
  reading it. `describe-alarms` returns `StateValue: OK` with a fresh datapoint. **Nothing in
  `observability.sh` is a deliverable of this story** — an implementer who takes the old Scope at face
  value will rebuild it and may double-publish the metric.
* **Only INFERENCE PROFILES are invokable**, and caching works on them. Plain on-demand
  `anthropic.claude-*` ids return `ValidationException: … on-demand throughput isn't supported`;
  `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` measured `cache_write=4017` then read on the next attempt
  [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550]. The verified id triple is checked in at
  `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
* **All three local gates already run clean on Bedrock** — `review-plan` (27/27 Bedrock calls,
  `cache_read` 226,668), `review-code` (5/5 Bedrock, `cache_read` 18,292), `verify-completion`
  (1/1 Bedrock, `cache_read` 45,122), all with structured output validating and zero direct-Anthropic
  calls [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7]. This cutover is a confirmation, not a first contact.
* **The parity bar is cleared as the epic defines it** [rebar:0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac]: same payloads,
  same tools, provider-clean routing, both inference profiles invoke. The operator hold recorded on
  this ticket ("DO NOT claim until 0d76 records a cleared bar") is therefore RELEASED. Carry the
  nuance: the residual `gating_failures` are informational cross-model verdict comparisons, so the
  slots read `passed=False` while no acceptance criterion is unmet.

## Approach

Fill the review-bot's **model-class slots** with Bedrock inference-profile ids, in the service's own
`environment:` block in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
      REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
      REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL: "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"
      REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL:  "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
```

These are the literal names in `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:105-115`. Because the gates name
classes rather than model ids, filling the slots re-points Pass-1 onto the Bedrock opus profile and
Pass-2/Pass-4 onto the Bedrock sonnet profile in one act, preserving the split that
[rebar:77ed-dea1-4997-4f74] restored and the standing operator rule behind it (standard is the default
for verification/judging; frontier needs justification). No `src/` change is expected. The ids are
copied from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` so there is exactly one authoritative triple, and a
test pins the two together so they cannot drift.

**The cutover is purely ADDITIVE and the kill switch is purely SUBTRACTIVE.** `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` appears
nowhere under `infra/` today (verified: `grep -rn REBAR_LLM_MODEL infra/` returns nothing), so the bot
currently runs on the built-in class defaults, which resolve to `anthropic:claude-*`. Deleting the three
lines above and recreating the container therefore restores the Anthropic path with no other edit —
the exact both-directions revert already proven token-free in [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] AC7.

**THE IMAGE DOES NOT INSTALL THE BEDROCK PROVIDER PACKAGE — a second, non-config deliverable.**
`infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:83` is `RUN uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra
reviewbot`, and `bedrock` is a **distinct extra** that is not in that list (`pyproject.toml:133-135`,
`bedrock = ["pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2"]`). `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:60-66` imports
`pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` and raises `LLMConfigError` when it is absent, so — with no
cross-provider fallback, deliberately — the class-slot flip ALONE would make the first Bedrock call
fail and the `LLM-Review` gate would stop voting on every landing on `main`. The fix is one flag: add
`--extra bedrock` to that `uv sync`.

*The gap is PARTIALLY masked, which is what defeats the obvious probe.* `pyproject.toml:93` is
`reviewbot = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]", "boto3"]`, so the container ALREADY has boto3, and both
region vars and IMDS credentials are already in place. Any probe of the form "can this container reach
Bedrock with boto3?" — including the boto3 region resolution that the provider builder itself
pre-checks at `bedrock_model.py:76-79` — therefore SUCCEEDS on an image that still lacks the provider
module. The dependency is partially satisfied, so the container reads as healthy right up to the first
gate call. The pre-cutover check must probe the IMPORT, not AWS reachability.

*Why this was invisible:* [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved all three gates clean on Bedrock (33
calls, zero direct-Anthropic) — but LOCALLY, in a dev env whose `[dev]` extra resolves
`pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,bedrock,openai,retries]`. A local proof cannot see a container packaging
gap.

*The lockfile does NOT need regenerating — checked, not assumed.* `uv.lock` already carries the bedrock
extra fully resolved: the `nava-rebar` entry has
`bedrock = [{ name = "pydantic-ai-slim", extra = ["bedrock"] }]`, and `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.1's own
`bedrock` extra resolves to `boto3==1.43.62`, already locked. `uv lock --check` passes against the
committed lock, and `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra reviewbot --extra bedrock
--dry-run` resolves with no drift complaint — so `--locked` is satisfied by the existing lock and no
`uv lock` regeneration is part of this story. One adjacency worth knowing: `uv.lock`'s `[conflicts]`
declares `bedrock` mutually exclusive with `eval` (and `dev` with `eval`); the image installs neither
`eval` nor `dev`, so adding `--extra bedrock` does not trip it.

**THE ANTHROPIC CREDENTIAL IS RETAINED. This story retires the DEFAULT USE, not the credential.**
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` is **out of scope and unchanged**, for two independent reasons:

1. *The kill switch needs it.* A recovery path that flips back to Anthropic without a key is a no-op,
   and it would be discovered at exactly the wrong moment. The credential must outlive the cutover.
2. *It is not per-container in the first place.* `fetch-secrets.sh:81` reads `anthropic-api-key` as a
   REQUIRED param and :116 writes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` into ONE shared `.env`, which is `env_file` for
   both `review-bot` (docker-compose.yml:113-114) and `opcert` (:196-197); opcert consumes it for its
   own gate LLM ops (:193). "Retire the key for this container" is not expressible against that layout,
   and deleting the line breaks opcert.

So the post-cutover container still carries `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, deliberately, unused. The old
acceptance criterion asserting the container env contains **no** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is **withdrawn**:
it contradicted the kill switch, and it was the wrong oracle anyway. The property actually worth
proving is positive and measurable — that no call on the Bedrock path reaches Anthropic — and
`REBAR_USAGE_LOG`'s per-call tally proves it directly, as it did for all three local gates.

**No cross-provider fallback**, unchanged from the original plan and still the right call: a
`FallbackModel` to direct Anthropic would mask exactly the failures this cutover exists to surface, and
a persistently degraded Bedrock could run unnoticed behind it. Note the asymmetry that makes this
coherent rather than dogmatic: the INTRA-provider fallback chain accepted in
[rebar:cc33-13db-de48-4468] (`model_classes.py:388`) stays available; it is only the cross-provider hop
that is refused.

**The transient-fault posture on Bedrock, stated accurately.** The original plan claimed "the existing
tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults". That is false on this path.
`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:88` is `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` and its docstring
says so explicitly: "No custom client/transport is opened here (unlike the retrying Anthropic path)".
There is no `botocore.config.Config(retries=…)`, no `"adaptive"` mode and no `aws_read_timeout`
anywhere in `src/rebar/llm/` — the tenacity envelope and `RetryConfig` live only in
`anthropic_model.py:114-150`. So:

* Bedrock's transient-fault handling is **botocore's stock client defaults**, which do retry throttling
  and transient 5xx, but are NOT configured by rebar and are NOT driven by `llm_retry_max_attempts` or
  `timeout_s`.
* The epic's "first_class = full fidelity ⇒ equivalent retry and timeout per transport" is an **unmet
  intention, not a landed property**. This story does not claim it and does not fix it: closing it means
  changing the provider builder, which belongs in a `src/` ticket rather than inside a production
  cutover. It is filed as its own defect, linked `discovered_from` this ticket, and the posture is
  written into the runbook so an operator debugging a throttle is not looking for a retry envelope that
  does not exist.
* Related honesty correction: inference profiles are **not** a throttling mitigation, which is how the
  original Approach justified them. Zero throttle events were observed across ~1,400 parity requests,
  the 33 local gate calls, and a 19-call plan-review. The evidenced reason is simpler and stronger —
  on-demand ids are not invokable at all [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550].

**Provenance oracle: `e951` is a hard prerequisite.** [rebar:343b-4fdc-6722-469b] delivered
`provider_provenance` for the plan-review and completion gates only. The code-review gate — the one
that produces the `LLM-Review` vote — still does not stamp it: `code_review/finalize.py:245` sets
`model` and nothing sets `provenance`, while `code_review/sidecar.py:106` reads
`verdict.get("provider_provenance")` and gets `None`. [rebar:e951-7df6-1851-4d5e] fixes exactly this
and is already implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 1307, so depending on it is cheap. The
`provider == "bedrock"` criterion below is gated on e951 landing; the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` tally is an
independent second observation that does not depend on it, so the cutover is not un-evidenced if e951
slips.

**Alternatives rejected**

* **`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` re-pointed at a Bedrock id** — the original plan's instrument. Rejected on three
  independent grounds: it is deprecated with a migration window [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00,
  rebar:d23e-1012-6749-4181], its deprecation shim fans a single value out to ALL THREE classes, which
  collapses the Pass-1/Pass-2 split back into one model, and a scalar cannot express a per-class mapping
  at all. Concretely: sonnet-everywhere silently downgrades the Pass-1 finder; opus-everywhere loses the
  Pass-2 cost downgrade and renders the `temperature: 0` greedy pin at `code-review.yaml:185`
  inoperative, since Bedrock opus accepts only the default temperature. Both single-model outcomes are
  wrong, in opposite directions. A runbook naming it would also rot at v1.0.0.
* **`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at `/app/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`** — genuinely
  attractive: it is the instrument [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] proved end-to-end, it is what the CI
  provider matrix uses, and it makes the id triple single-sourced by construction. Rejected for the
  container specifically. The file is present in the image only incidentally —
  `Dockerfile.reviewbot:82` is `COPY . /app` and `.dockerignore` happens not to exclude `.github` — so a
  future context-trimming change would delete it and the pointer would fail at gate time in production,
  after the deploy that caused it. Env class slots also OUTRANK the file pointer in the precedence order
  (CLI > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered file > default), so keeping both layers live invites
  two configurations that silently disagree. The single-sourcing benefit is recovered by the drift test
  instead of by indirection.
* **Per-service Anthropic key retirement via a `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""` override in the review-bot
  `environment:` block** — technically expressible (compose `environment:` outranks `env_file`), and it
  would satisfy the old "no Anthropic credential in this container" criterion without touching opcert.
  Rejected because it disables the kill switch for the sake of a criterion we have withdrawn, and buys
  nothing: the credential is unused either way, and "unused" is what the usage-log tally proves.

## Scope

- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — the three class-slot env vars in the `review-bot` service's
  `environment:` block. Region vars are already present and are not re-added.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — add `--extra bedrock` to the `uv sync --locked` line (:83),
  so the image contains `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock`. No `uv.lock` edit accompanies it (see
  Approach: the lock already resolves that extra and `--locked` is already satisfied).
- `infra/terraform/` — a Bedrock `InvokeModel` client-error alarm built on AWS/Bedrock NATIVE metrics via
  a `metric_query` metric-math expression, NOT a host-published custom metric. MEASURED in this account:
  the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace already publishes `InvocationClientErrors` and `Invocations`, dimensioned by
  `ModelId` (values include `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` from this epic's own traffic), so the rate is
  computable as `InvocationClientErrors / Invocations` with no publisher to add. THIS IS WHY
  `observability.sh` STAYS OUT OF SCOPE: the alternative — a `rebar/host` custom metric — would require a
  new publisher there and would re-open a scope claim this plan deliberately makes. It also means the
  DIMENSIONLESS-ON-BOTH-SIDES contract that `monitoring_s4b.tf` and `monitoring_s5.tf` document does not
  apply here: those are host-published custom metrics, whereas a native metric is dimensioned by AWS and
  the alarm must MATCH that dimensioning (`ModelId`) rather than avoid it. State the dimension explicitly
  in the resource so it cannot silently stop matching.
  This is the one signal the existing
  `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm cannot give: `voter_errors` fires only when the gate fails to vote
  at all, so a partially degraded Bedrock that still produces votes is invisible to it. Thresholds per
  the epic's criterion (client-error rate > 25% of invocations over a 15-minute window, 2 consecutive
  periods), with the alarm ARN and a forced test notification recorded on this ticket — the evidence
  gap the epic's AC has been carrying unresolved.
- `infra/runbooks/` — the kill-switch entry (class slots, not `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`), stating that the
  Anthropic credential is retained by design and why, and recording the actual Bedrock retry/timeout
  posture.
- a test pinning the compose class-slot values to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.
- **NOT in scope:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (see Approach), `infra/scripts/observability.sh`
  (already shipped under S4b), and any `src/rebar/llm/` change — including the botocore retry/timeout
